metadata.title: Running / Building — Giorgio Pedezzi
metadata.description: A small visual language for a moving human being.
metadata.socialDescription: A small visual language for a moving human being.

hero.label: Running / Building
hero.heading: The runner enlightens the data.
hero.intro: Without the runner, there is telemetry. With the runner, the data acquires meaning.

problem.label: The problem
problem.heading: More metrics do not automatically create more understanding.
problem.body: A running plan can look precise while still missing the person who has to live it. Information is useful only when it helps a runner make sense of what is happening.

restraint.label: A deliberate restraint
restraint.heading: Not another dashboard asking to be obeyed.
restraint.body: This is not an attempt to reproduce every metric, build a universal coach, or turn running into a compliance exercise. It makes room for interpretation while keeping the objective in view.

principles.label: Principles
principles.heading: A system should assist without taking the runner out of the picture.

items.text: The runner remains at the centre.

object.label: The object
object.heading: A small visual language for a moving human being.
object.body: The visual study below is not a product dashboard. It explains the idea: heart-rate intensity moves from pink towards red; a long pause lets the runner collapse, while a short one keeps them jogging in place.

study.title: A body, not a spreadsheet
study.label: A visual study
study.body: The figure gives the telemetry a subject. The data is still there, but it no longer pretends to be the whole story.

build.label: How it is being built
build.heading: AI coding agents, under human direction.
build.body: The implementation is often delegated to AI coding agents. The concept, constraints, priorities and decisions remain human work. That division is part of the experiment.

state.label: Current state
state.heading: A living experiment.
state.body: The project is still being shaped in public-facing fragments. This page records the thinking behind it without claiming a finished product where one does not yet exist.

liveApp.label: Want to play a little bit with it?
